text:
RESOLVED BY THE SCRIPT'S OWN INSTRUMENTATION. I ran 05 as written - no modification, no reconstruction - with UNCERTAINTY_NODES=25. Its own per-node timer reports:

  sampling covariance: 16.2 s total, 0.65 s/node mean
    first 10 nodes: 0.64 s/node, RSS 782 MB
    last 10 nodes : 0.57 s/node, RSS 557 MB

0.65 s/node, not ~9 s/node. At that rate the full 577-centre sweep is about 6.3 minutes, not 90.

THE THREE CLAIMS IN THIS BEAD'S TITLE, checked against that output:

  "~7 s/node"                 NOT REPRODUCED. 0.65 s/node by the script's own clock, and
                              0.455 s/node by my independent reconstruction of the loop body.
                              Two methods, same order.
  "appears to leak across
   calls"                     REFUTED by the script's own RSS instrumentation. Per-node time
                              FALLS 0.64 -> 0.57 s and RSS FALLS 782 -> 557 MB across the run.
                              Both move the wrong way for a leak.
  ">1 h for a 577-node sweep" NOT REPRODUCED. 577 x 0.65 s is about 6.3 minutes.

"single-node-only" still holds - the function does evaluate one frame node per call - but that is a design property, not a defect, and at 0.65 s/node it is not the problem the bead describes.

WHY MY FIRST ATTEMPT LOOKED WORSE, since it is misleading in the log above: I ran the whole script under a 600 s limit and it exceeded it, which reads as confirmation of the bead. It is not. The script's own breakdown shows the covariance loop was 16.2 s of that. The remaining time is data loading, the 577-centre searchlight frame build, the consistency RDM over all centres, and arms C and D. Timing a whole script and attributing the total to one function inside it is the same mistake I made twice earlier today, and I nearly made it a third time.

ONE VERIFIED-GOOD FROM THE SAME RUN, worth recording because it is the arm's central claim:

  refit RDM vs 02's precomputed-mean RDM: max abs difference = 4.44e-16

The error-channel refit reproduces the point-estimate arm to machine epsilon. That is the guard the script says it needs - that the error bars belong to the estimate they are attached to - and it holds exactly.

WHAT I CANNOT ESTABLISH: when this changed. The bead was filed at 01:38 with a field observation; the tree has moved since. It is entirely possible the figure was accurate when written and a change has landed since, or that the original run differed in some way I have not reconstructed. I am reporting the current measured state, not adjudicating the original.

SUGGESTED DISPOSITION: close or heavily downgrade this bead, and correct the exemplar README Cost section, which currently tells users the arm defaults to 120 nodes at about 22 minutes and that all 577 takes about 90 minutes. On this measurement 120 nodes is about 80 seconds and all 577 about 6 minutes. That section is the only place a user learns what the error-channel arm costs, and it currently overstates it by more than an order of magnitude - which would deter people from using the capability the whole epic was built to provide.
